number_of_offences: Multiple counts charged, but the final upheld conviction was for murder under Section 302 IPC
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the testimony of PW-1 as the sole eye witness but found it unreliable due to inconsistencies and unnatural conduct.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as unreliable, noting that PW-1's conduct was unnatural and inconsistent with human behavior, and that PW-11 and PW-5 turned hostile.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 03.08.1990; Trial judgment: 09.05.2014; High Court decision: Not stated; Supreme Court decision: October 12, 2020
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Ms. Aishwarya Bhati, Dushyant Dave, Sr.Adv., Nikhil Goel, Ms. Naveen Goel, Dushyant Sarna, Vinay Mathew, Rishi Malhotra, Ms. Rashmi Malhotra, Sachin Sharma, S.K.Tyagi; Counsel for the State: B. V. Balaram Das, V.K.Malik, Rahul Raj Malik, Aftab Ali Khan, Advs.
investigation_status: Investigation conducted by Inspector Richpal Singh, case registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
procedural_irregularity: The tip of the knife recovered was broken and not pointed, and the medical expert was not shown the weapon to give an opinion on whether the injuries could have been caused by it
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted under Section 302 IPC r/w Section 34 IPC; High Court: Dismissed the appeal; Supreme Court: Allowed the appeals, set aside the impugned orders
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused persons attacked the victim with hockey sticks and a knife, and that the victim was declared dead by a doctor after being taken to the hospital. The trial court convicted the accused under Section 302 IPC r/w Section 34 IPC and sentenced them to life imprisonment.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution's case was based on the solitary testimony of an eye witness, PW-1, who was not corroborated by other witnesses. They also pointed out inconsistencies in the medical evidence and the conduct of the witnesses, suggesting that PW-1 was not present at the scene and that the prosecution's story was improbable.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that the testimony of a single eye witness can be relied upon if found reliable, but if there are doubts about the testimony, corroboration is necessary. The court also emphasized the importance of eliciting the opinion of a medical witness regarding the cause of injuries and the weapon used.
precedent_relied_upon: Kartarey and Ors. v. State of U.P. (1976) 1 SCC 172; Ishwar Singh v. State of U.P. (1976) 4 SCC 355; Selvaraj v. The State of Tamil Nadu (1976) 4 SCC 343
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was not imposed because the court found the prosecution's case to be unreliable and the conviction based on the sole testimony of an eye witness who was not corroborated. The court set aside the conviction and ordered the release of the appellants.
